messages.author: 7374fce48170779f
messages.subject: A question about prediction using inla()
parts:
Hi, 

I want to do spatio-temporal prediction using inla(), suppose I have two datasets:

First one with y values from time period 3 set to NA for prediction:

   x1  x2  y   time_period
1  4   3   5.32      1
2  6   6   3.65      1
3  4   2   8.74      2
4  6   8   3.64      2
5  4   2   na        3
6  6   7   na        3

The second dataset has the same x1 and x2 columns but with y values from time periods 3 and 4 set to NA:

   x1  x2  y   time_period
1  4   3   5.32      1
2  6   6   3.65      1
3  4   2   8.74      2
4  6   8   3.64      2
5  4   2   na        3
6  6   7   na        3
7  4   5   na        4
8  6   9   na        4

If I run the model using these two datasets separately, will the prediction values for time period 3 from these two model results be the same? And why?

Thanks!

Chris

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] A question about prediction using inla()
parts:
yes, up to numerical accuracy.

> n = 10
> y = arima.sim(n, model = list(ar = 0.9))
> N = 20
> yy = c(y, rep(NA,N-n))
> r = inla(yy ~ -1 + f(time, model="ar1"), control.predictor =
list(compute=TRUE), data = data.frame(time=1:N,yy=yy))
> N = 200
> yy = c(y, rep(NA,N-n))
> rr = inla(yy ~ -1 + f(time, model="ar1"), control.predictor =
list(compute=TRUE), data = data.frame(time=1:N,yy=yy))
> r$summary.linear.predictor$mean[11:20]
[1] 0.091009511104 0.061937250228 0.043946208314 0.032369166729
0.024631535028
[6] 0.019272438726 0.015442771564 0.012634614284 0.010529591632
0.008921194799
> rr$summary.linear.predictor$mean[11:20]
[1] 0.091010217888 0.061937912457 0.043946694180 0.032369483470
0.024631731395
[6] 0.019272547899 0.015442827579 0.012634642222 0.010529609588
0.008921215252
